newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine oil refinery bankruptcy hearing postponed.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine oil refinery bankruptcy hearing postponed.

text.p: Ukraine will begin hearings next month on whether the country's second largest oil refinery is bankrupt, a step that could spur its privatisation, a spokesman for the State Oil and Gas Committee said on Thursday.

Stepan Yaloveha told Reuters that court hearings on the Lisichansk refinery were due to start this week in the Poltava regional court in central Ukraine, but that management had asked the government to postpone the hearings until November.

"The essence of the matter is very old and complicated in nature," Yaloveha said by telephone. "Several years ago, the plant had received oil but after refining the oil, the refined products disappeared somewhere."
The plant, in eastern Ukraine, is due to be privatised this year.
It has an annual capacity of 16 million tonnes, but refined only 1.1 million tonnes in the first six months of this year.
Sources in the committee said the Kiev-based Agrocomplex company gave 200,000 tonnes of oil, worth $30 million, to the Lisichansk refinery in 1993.
"Now the company which sent the unrefined oil to Lisichansk wants the products back or to be paid for the oil, and has taken the case to court," Yaloveha said.
He said two fates could await the refinery.
Under one proposal, Ukraine could award Russia a 40 percent stake in the plant if its neighbour agrees to supply it with at least seven million tonnes of Russian oil annually over seven years.
Another possibility is for Italian and Austrian banks to step in with financing.
Interfax Ukraine news agency said the refinery owed $40 million to various creditors, including Westdeutsche Landesbank AG.
Ukraine's six refineries routinely processed up to 60 million tonnes of crude a year in the Soviet era, but last year refined only 16.8 million tonnes as Russian crude supplies tailed off.
